taxonomyNote: Once treated as the same species as the kit fox; NatureServe treats V. macrotis as separate.
fieldMarks: Small fox with a black-tipped tail and black patches on either side of the snout
Winter coat dark buffy gray above, orange-tan on sides, legs and underside of tail; summer coat shorter and more reddish
Throat, chest, belly and inside of ears creamy white
Differs from kit fox in smaller ears, broader snout and shorter tail
behavior: Primarily nocturnal; may rest in the sun outside the burrow by day
Dens in burrows it digs or takes over from other mammals
Opportunistic diet: jackrabbits, cottontails, ground squirrels, mice, birds, invertebrates, grasses, berries; caches food under snow in winter
habitat: Open prairie and arid plains, mainly shortgrass prairie; often digs dens in sandy soil, along fences or in plowed fields.
range: Historically the central plains from southern Alberta and Saskatchewan to northern Texas, including southern Manitoba; present range is much restricted, nearly continuous from Wyoming south through eastern Colorado, western Kansas, the Oklahoma Panhandle and eastern New Mexico.

lookalikes.name: Kit fox
lookalikes.howToTell: Larger ears, narrower snout, longer tail; more arid southwestern range.
